Subsequently, we delved into the RCNN [7] family of algorithms and the YOLO [8], [9]family of algorithms for both two-phase target detection algorithms and single-phase target detection algorithms. We used manually annotated datasets to train the relevant models and tested these algorithms for performance evaluation in task scenarios. In the end, we chose the YOLOv7 and StrongSORT [9], [13] based algorithms to successfully implement the personnel counting task and achieved a small error through model optimization to make it suitable for complex scenarios.

articleTitle: KCPE-SMDI:Key Contour Points Extraction Method Based on Stroke Multi-Dimensional Information for Chinese Character Vectorization
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The vectorization of Chinese characters is very important for the industrial design and manufacture, the digitization of characters, and the generation of handwritten font libraries. However, when most of the general vectorization methods and Chinese character vectorization methods are vectorizing Chinese characters, the vector Chinese characters will have edge bending problems due to the jitter noise at the edges of the Chinese characters. If we remove the jitter noise on the edge by reducing the overall threshold, some small features of the Chinese characters will be lost at the same time. And the key points of the generated Chinese character vector graphics will be redundant. Therefore, this paper proposes key contour points extraction method based on stroke multi-dimensional information for Chinese character vectorization (KCPE-SMDI). Through multi-dimensional information such as Chinese character stroke type, Chinese character key skeleton points and stroke width, the key contour points of Chinese characters are extracted, and the jitter noise contour points and redundant contour points are removed. Using multiple groups of Chinese character raster images, we compared the vectorization results of our method(KCPE-SMDI) with four different methods. The experiments showed that our method not only reduces the number of contour points by 8.0419% compared with the current method of generating the minimum contour points(Wang et al. method), but also solves the problem of edge bending of vectorized Chinese characters and maintains the feature of the original Chinese characters.

articleTitle: Context-Aware API Recommendation for Mashup Composition Based on Path Ranking
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In recent years, more software modules have been increasingly published onto the Internet as web APIs, making the activity of manually composing mashups time-consuming and error-prone for mashup developers. In both academia and industry, discovering and recommending suitable web APIs has become a core method to increase the working efficiency for mashup developers. In this paper, we propose a novel context-aware approach based on path ranking algorithm (PRA) to recommending next potential APIs in a recommend-as-you-go manner. At every step throughout the process of composing a mashup, the APIs that have been selected and the collection of words in the textually described requirement are regarded as contextual input of a prediction model which is comprised of weights of various relation paths being built from a relation schema. Given the input query, candidate APIs are ranked in descending order according to its predicted score of being the API that should be selected at next step. Finally, top K of these candidate APIs are recommended to the mashup developer. Extensive experiments on a real-world dataset demonstrate that our approach is effective.

articleTitle: Uyghur Language Off-line Signature Verification Based On The Modified Directional Features
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In this paper, in order to compensate the blank of ethnic minorities off-line signature verification system in our country, firstly it is conducted a set of preprocessing steps such as, graying, binarization, smoothing, and normalization for the collected Uyghur language signature images having combined with the Uyghur language handwritten signature writing style and characteristics. Then, based on the traditional direction feature extraction method, the signature sample images were divided into a rectangular area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 4$</tex> after preprocessing, and it is proposed modified 48 dimensional features based on the information in the signatures image pixels within each region and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^\circ, 3 0^\circ, 6 0^\circ, 90^\circ, 120, 150^\circ$</tex> direction. Finally, three kinds of distance classifiers were used and experimental results were analyzed and evaluated using 900 Uygur signature samples collected from 15 person (20samples/per person), and the total correct rate of signature reached 96.00%. This indicates that, for off line Uyghur handwritten signature verification, the modified 48 dimensional direction feature is an effective feature, which can better reflect the writing style and characteristics of Uyghur language handwriting signature.

articleTitle: Cryptographic Reverse Firewall for Digital Signature in Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Fog computing (FC) is introduced as an extended technique of cloud computing. FC makes it possible to compute straightly on the brim of the network. In FC application systems, authentication is an important security requirement when fog nodes communicate with other fog devices. Digital signature (DS) has been widely used in FC systems to provide the non-repudiation, authenticity along with data integrity. However, some latest research results demonstate that DS schemes may confront the algorithm substitution attack (ASA). That is, DS scheme would be implanted some covert backdoor information in algorithm implementation process by attackers. With the backdoor information attackers can recover the secret key of fog devices' users, which will result in privacy disclosure. To settle this matter, the notion of cryptographic reverse firewall (CRF) is proposed, which can re-randomize the inputs and outputs of the fog devices. Moreover, due to the limited storing and computing abilities of fog devices, the DS algorithms applied to FC systems should be resource-saving. In this paper, we simultaneously focus attention on addressing above two problems in fog computing and construct the CRFs for the Camenisch and Lysyanskaya DS scheme (CL signature) which is suitable to be applied in FC systems because of its high efficiency.

articleTitle: Semi − Disambiguated Partial Label Learning by Mixing Disambiguation and Non-disambiguation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Partial Label Learning (PLL) is employed to tackle the issue of ambiguous labeling, where each instance in the training set is associated with a set of labels, but only one label in the associated set is the ground-true label. Two common strategies, disambiguation and non-disambiguation, both achieve some improvements in tackling the PLL problem. However, they each have their own drawbacks. In this work, we develop a novel PLL method, namely, Semi-Disambiguated Partial Label Learning (SDPLL), to mix the two strategies with the goal of enhancing the strengths and making up for the weaknesses of both strategies. In specific, first we adapt label propagation to operate a coarse-level disambiguation, by which we eliminate low-confidence labels from the candidate label set to get the shrinking set of candidate labels. Next, we employ binary decomposition to conduct non-disambiguation treatment on the shrinking version of the dataset. Empirical experiments on both controlled UCI datasets and real-world datasets justify the superiority (at least the competitiveness) of SDPLL over several representative competing models.

articleTitle: MFYOLO: An Improved YOLOv5 Algorithm for Small Target Detection in UAV-Captured Images
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: With the advancement of unmanned aerial vehicles, the detection of small targets has become a crucial task. However, it is challenging due to the complexity of the scenes and the small size of the targets. In recent years, various object detection methods based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) have made significant progress in small target detection. Despite these advancements, these methods still suffer from a high false detection rate, as well as substantial time and computational overhead, resulting in unsatisfactory performance. Therefore, we propose a multi-fusion YOLOv5 method (MFYOLO) in this paper, which incorporates attention blocks and a multi-scale feature fusion structure to enhance feature fusion and extraction capabilities. To evaluate our proposed method, we conducted extensive comparative experiments on the challenging VisDrone2019 dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the mAP@0.5 is significantly improved by 10.0% from the original.

articleTitle: Human Motion Prediction via Adaptive Fusing Autoregressive and Non-Autoregressive Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Human motion prediction is a challenging task that aims to predict future human poses based on an observed historical pose sequence. Previous approaches typically use an encoder-decoder model to extract spatiotemporal features of human motion, decode features and generate future poses either in an autoregressive or non-autoregressive manner. The former suffers from the issue of error accumulation, resulting in poor long-term predictions. The latter does not explicitly model temporal dependencies between predicted frames, which may adversely affect overall quality. To address the above issues, in this paper, we propose a novel hybrid framework combining autoregressive and non-autoregressive fashions. It employs a multi-branch parallel architecture to capture temporal dependencies at various time scales and the multi-head self-attention mechanism to encode spatial correlations among different body joints. Besides, we design a time-adaptive fusion module to integrate prediction outputs from each branch. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach by surpassing previous state-of-the-art methods on two benchmark datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/aill/AFANAT.

articleTitle: Computing and Tracing Particle on Surface of Overlapping AMR
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The computation on the surface of Overlapping Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) is exclusively performed within the non-Overlapping zone of its multi-level patch-based mesh — a distinctive computing mode for Overlapping AMR. Effectuating surface computing based on Overlapping AMR necessitates the reciprocal mapping of two computing modes: Overlapping AMR multi-level computing and non-Overlapping AMR computing. This study consolidates the mapping relationship between these two modes into data mapping, algorithm mapping, and parallel unit mapping. Subsequently, solutions are proposed for the implementation of these mappings, thereby establishing a foundational method for conducting surface computing using Overlapping AMR. Building upon this foundation, the present article utilizes tracing particles on the surface of Overlapping AMR as a paradigm, elucidating how to leverage the aforementioned mapping relationships to construct a surface tracing particle function within our center's JASMIN (J parallel Adaptive Structured Mesh applications INfrastructure). Additionally, a corresponding method for drawing tracing particle trajectories is provided. Functional testing of these elements demonstrates that the application effects of the functions align with expectations. The successful realization of surface tracing particles based on multi-level AMR attests to the completeness of the three aforementioned mappings, providing guidance for practical algorithmic endeavors. The amalgamation of multi-level computing and surface computing based on overlapping AMR empowers users to consider diverse factors such as numerical format, interpolation format, and application performance. This capability enables users to construct applications tailored to their specific requirements, fostering the development of ideal applications.

articleTitle: A Temporal Difference Pyramid Network for Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The visual rhythm of human actions can distinguish human actions with high visual similarity by expressing the dynamic and rhythmic scales of activities. In traditional convolutional neural networks, most of the input videos are sampled at different rates using local receptive fields, and there are also methods using multi-layer networks to process videos at different rates, but this requires high computational costs and additional computational resources. The previous methods cannot deal with the problem of feature fusion between different levels of features when identifying the relationship between visual speed and high-level attributes and fine-grained rhythm. In our study, we propose a Temporal Difference Pyramid Network (TDPN). What is significantly extracted from the action recognition network is multi-layer backbone features. The two key points are the global temporal modeling module and the local temporal modeling module. The global temporal modeling module is responsible for extracting low-level features with more location information, while the local temporal modeling module is responsible for extracting high-level features with more semantic information. Meanwhile, a multi-head self-attention mechanism has been used to simultaneously focus on different levels of feature information, better capturing the relative relationships between different features in the video sequence. Then, by aggregating different levels of features, the pixel-level fine-grained rhythm dynamics of action visual rhythm with rich information is obtained. Tests on various action recognition benchmarks, including Something-Something V1 and V2 and Kinetics-400, have shown that the TDPN network we suggested significantly boosts the performance of the current video-based action recognition model.

articleTitle: Interval-Valued Z-Number Aggregation Operators and Its Application in Airbus Type Selection Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: This article introduces interval-valued Z-number with interval and linguistic value. It is a reliable tool to explain the vagueness or unclear boundary of linguistic in multiple attribute group decision making. This article uses linguistic scale functions to compute interval-valued with linguistic. Firstly, the operations of IVZN are defined, therefore two types of aggregation operators are proposed to aggregate information. The ranking result are calculated through the score function and accuracy function. Finally, an example of airbus type selection is used to further verify the practicability of the method.

articleTitle: Fusion of Enhancing Target Features and Focusing Slice Features for Soil Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Soil classification based on the identification of soil surface and physical properties is a key point in calculating indicators such as stability, bearing capacity, and uniformity of construction sites in soil exploration. In this paper, soil image classification is regarded as a sub task of fine-grained image classification, and a soil image classification algorithm model integrating target feature enhancement and slice feature focusing is proposed. This model constructs a three branch network for Supervised learning. First, the backbone network obtains the overall characteristics of the image; Then, the image position is obtained through cross level feature fusion to reduce background noise interference and enhance target features; Finally, based on the feature mapping relationship of the target image, a local region with the highest degree of differentiation and the lowest degree of redundancy is proposed to achieve slice feature focusing. The proposed model has achieved competitive results on CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, FGVC-Aircraft and Soil.

articleTitle: Geometric-Aware Facial Landmark Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Emotion recognition is crucial for enhancing human-computer interaction. While traditional approaches largely depend on RGB images, our proposed Geometric-Aware Facial Landmark Emotion Recognition framework harnesses the geometric and spectral attributes of facial landmarks for emotion recognition. This work unfolds three key contributions: utilizing Graph Convolutional Networks to grasp the natural spatial relationships among facial landmarks, introducing distance-aware graph operations to accentuate the relational geometry, and employing spectral encodings to comprehend the frequency-based attributes of landmark positions. Through rigorous experiments on recognized datasets RAF-DB and KDEF, Our method surpasses baseline methods, demonstrating its effectiveness especially in high-resolution scenarios where detailed facial landmarks are apparent. The datasets curated for Facial Landmark Emotion Recognition will also be shared publicly as part of this work, offering a significant resource for the community. The encouraging results highlight the potential of geometric-aware analysis in propelling emotion recognition systems forward, opening avenues for further research in this evolving domain.

articleTitle: TDS: Two Diffusion Streams for Low-Light Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Low-light image enhancement is a challenging task aimed at improving the visibility of low-light images, and the results obtained from previous methods still have shortcomings in terms of detail recovery and overall quality. Recently, diffusion models have shown impressive ability in generating realistic and detailed images through a multi-step denoising refinement process, which motivates us to introduce them into low-light image enhancement for higher quality results. However, we found in experiments that using a diffusion model to enhance low-light images leads to color distortion in the restored results. To address this issue, we propose a model called Two Diffusion Streams (TDS). It employs a dual-stream architecture, where one stream is used to initially enhance the low-light image and reconstruct its structure, while the other stream utilizes the color map for color correction. The experimental results on existing benchmark datasets demonstrate that our model not only resolves the color distortion issue but also produces higher-quality results with fewer noise and artifacts. Additionally, it exhibits stronger generalization capability across different scenes.

articleTitle: Calculation Strategy of Improved Genetic Algorithm Based on Growth Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: To improve the optimization characteristics of genetic algorithm, this paper presents a growth-mechanism calculation strategy, that is, in each iteration of genetic population, a group of new individuals are generated in the neighborhood of a set of optimal values to replace the poor individuals in the population, so as to update the population. On the one hand, the individuals generated in the neighborhood of excellent individuals have the relevant attributes of excellent individuals, which can ensure the correctness of the optimization direction of the population. On the other hand, the neighborhood search also expands the range of optimization of the population and diversifies the population, so as to avoid falling into local optimization. The growth-mechanism calculation strategy involves three factors, including how many outstanding individuals are selected for inheritance, the size of the neighborhood, and how many individuals are eliminated from the population. In this paper, genetic factor, carrier probability and evolutionary weight are used to define the above three factors. The article verifies that the growth-mechanism genetic algorithm is superior to a single genetic algorithm by taking the example of finding the optimal value of a quadratic function. By designing different calculation cases, the influence of the genetic factor, carrier probability, evolution weight, population size and number of calculations on the calculation of the growth-mechanism genetic algorithm is discussed. The study finds that the growth-mechanism calculation strategy can greatly enhance the sensitivity of the population to the optimal solution and can effectively improve the optimization efficiency and convergence speed of the genetic algorithm. The three influencing factors have a great influence on the optimization calculation results. Setting the values of the three influencing factors reasonably can greatly improve the optimization efficiency. Although the smaller the value of the carrier probability is, the higher the optimization efficiency, this value is affected by the range of variables, and there is an optimal genetic factor and an optimal evolution weight in the calculation of the growth-mechanism genetic algorithm. In this paper, when calculating the optimal value of a quadratic function, it is found that the optimal result is obtained when the genetic factor is 0.8 and the evolution weight is 0.5. In addition, as the population size and number of calculations increase, the optimization calculation results improve, however, after reaching a certain value, the optimization result peaks, and increasing the population size and number of calculations will waste calculation time. Therefore, a reasonable setting of the population size and number of calculations will help improve the efficiency of optimization calculations.

articleTitle: Contextualized Word Embeddings via Generative Adversarial Learning of Syntagmatic and Paradigmatic Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: In this work, we propose a general regularized function-learning framework of contextualized word embeddings, named Generative Adversarial Learning of Syntagmatic and Paradigmatic structure of Context (GAL-SPC), aiming to build word embeddings via the trainable encoder function based on the distributional structure. What makes a difference is the context of a given word is viewed as a connected graph so that the context-level syntagmatic structure and the document-level statistical pattern can be formalized as a vocabulary co-occurrence matrix. Meanwhile, to better integrate the paradigmatic structure, GAL-SPC exploits posteriori approach based on edit distance and prior approach based on knowledge base to pick paradigmatic contexts with substitutable words and regularizes the training of autoencoder via generative adversarial learning process to better model the syntagmatic and paradigmatic structure of contexts. Finally, we trained GAL-SPC with a public wikipedia corpus, and the intrinsic evaluations with word analogy and similarity tasks and the extrinsic evaluations with document clustering and classification tasks demonstrates that GAL-SPC outperforms other comparative methods.

articleTitle: Group Sparse Radiomics Representation Network for Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease Using Triple Graph Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: Brain network have been widely used in the study of brain abnormalities in Alzheimer's disease (AD). The construction of network is important for brain characterization and graph neural networks (GNNs)-based classification tasks. Currently, structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI)-based structural covariance networks usually only consider interactions between pairs of brain regions at the individual level, and do not take into account higher-order relationships between multiple brain regions or subjects. To overcome these limitations, we proposed the group sparse radiomics representation network (GSR2N) which utilizes group sparse representation (GSR) instead of traditional Pearson correlation (PC) construction method. This reduces inter-individual differences in network topology and accounts for mixing effects among multiple brain regions. We conducted extensive experiments using the ADNI and AIBL dataset on triple graph convolutional network (TGCN) to compare the classification performance of different network construction methods. The results demonstrate that GSR method has the highest classification performance, with intra and inter-dataset test accuracies of 0.894 and 0.856, respectively. This new approach is expected to contribute to future sMRI-based brain network construction and brain disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Calibration Method of Industrial Robot Kinematic Parameters Based on Improved SSA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Software Engineering and Computer Science (CSECS)
abstract: The requirements of high-end manufacturing cannot be fulfilled by industrial robot absolute positioning accuracy. A study of algorithms for improving absolute positioning accuracy in industrial robots. An improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA) incorporating a chaotic mapping initialization population, a butterfly global search strategy, a triangle wandering strategy, and a t-distribution perturbation is proposed to identify the kinematic parameters of industrial robots. First, a robot kinematics model is established based on modified Denavit-Hartenberg (MD-H) parameters. Secondly, verify the effectiveness of the ISSA algorithm. Finally, the kinematic parameters of four T6A-19 industrial robots were determined and adjusted for validation using the ISSA algorithm. The results of the experiment demonstrate an 85.39% improvement in the accuracy of the mean absolute positional error and an 83.36% improvement in the root mean square accuracy. These results support the effectiveness and practicality of the method used.
